summary: Re-run after the Green r7 tokenizer remediation (fde3eda2): the sweep is no longer blind for any briefed form. Adv 10 and adv 11, the committed guards for the r3 defects F1r3 (CRLF) and F2r3 (in-string /*), now pass live, so both blockers are withdrawn. The re-check of adv 1 to 12 passes, and the r4 attack set (about 30 seeded forms under apps/integrated-math-3, each with a live oxlint probe against the exact tokenizer logic of the test file) found no new hole: every honored form (shebang in .js and .mjs, BOM, .mjs, .cjs, template substitution, the JSX expression container in .js and .tsx, a regex holding \/* above a real disable, the mid-line type-annotation form, adjacent-token trivia) is counted exactly once and stripped with the finding surfaced; the unhonored spellings (uppercase, mixed case, a spaced hyphen, a U+2011 hyphen, regex text) stay live and the pin counts none of them; a comment-only file counts through the end-of-file token; parse-broken files (a syntax error, an unterminated comment) stay loud in the original and the stripped copy, and oxlint applies no rule finding to a parse-error file, so nothing hides there. The 49-carrier sweep replica at this HEAD reports 43 files with surfaced findings, 86 decoded rules, 0 missing, 0 extras, and no parse diagnostic. Two Nits remain (the SOURCE_EXT_RE extension-set coupling and a classify quirk); both default to accept and neither opens a hole. The new adv 13 pins the verified-good forms and the unhonored spellings as live regression tripwires (commit b9a4f0c2).
nonblocking_findings: F1r4 [Nit] adversarial-testing: SOURCE_EXT_RE (scripts/__tests__/oxc-toolchain-gates.test.ts:984) hardcodes the extension set {js,jsx,mjs,cjs,ts,tsx} that the root config override globs also hardcode. Live probes show a bare .mts or .cts file exits 0 under the root config (no rule applies to it), so the scan's exclusion is consistent today and nothing can hide in an .mts or .cts file. But no guard ties the two sets together: a later config change that adds .mts or .cts to an override glob would lint those files while lintedFilesWithDisableDirectives and the adv 7 sweep stay blind to their carriers. The pin covers a listed carrier of any parsed extension (allowlistPinViolations parses by entry.path), but the scan never lists such a carrier. No hole exists today. Default disposition: note only; no change in this phase.

F2r4 [Nit] adversarial-testing: directiveKindsOfFile classifies a block comment whose text merely contains 'disable-line' as trailing (scripts/__tests__/oxc-toolchain-gates.test.ts:1064-1069; live probe: the span '/* eslint-disable // eslint-disable-line */' decodes kinds=[trailing], blocks=0). A blanket disable whose comment text mentions disable-line in prose therefore counts as a trailing directive and adds no blanket block, so the blanket-growth clause does not cover that specific shape. The kinds and directive-count clauses still fail on any change to such a file, so no hole exists. Default disposition: accept; no helper change.
